title: Deuce Point
intro: A point lasts about six seconds. Then you get about twenty-five before the next one, and every other game there's a ninety second changeover. This session squeezes that shape down: six sprints, a long breather, six more. The twenty-fourth effort is the one that matters. Each game is its own card, so you'll see Shuttle Sprint four times. Time the rests on a watch. Four games of six sprints. Ten metres out and ten back, as fast as you can control, with one hard turn at the far end. Twenty-five seconds between each one and ninety between games. That twenty-five seconds is the session. It isn't enough on purpose, so don't stretch it. You need twenty metres of flat, dry ground with real grip and a few metres clear at each end. Mark the far end ten metres out with tape or a line on the floor, not something you could step on. Wear court shoes or trainers with grip, and skip wet grass and polished floors. Padel points run longer, so padel players run the out and back twice without stopping, about twelve seconds, with the same rest. Do that only once the normal version feels easy to control.

First time through, run the first game at about three quarters speed and stop after two games. Keep it 48 hours clear of a match, of heavy lower-body lifting, of Hard Stop and Cut & Recover in the On-Court list, and of any other hard running session, on either side. Leave it out of a tournament week. If you have a sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles right now, or an injury has kept you off court in the last month, this isn't the session for today, so get it looked at first. Stop the session and get it checked if you get a sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop at the back of your thigh, in your groin, your calf or your Achilles. Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right means stop now and get it looked at before you train again. If a doctor has told you to be careful with hard exercise, check with them before you do this one. If you are far more sore than normal a day or two later, or your pee goes dark, get that checked the same day.

before.text: Run the first game at about three quarters speed and stop after two games.

good: Easy pace until you are warm and breathing
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
The swing should get a little bigger every rep
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Step long, drop the back hip, then reach the inside arm up to the ceiling
Feel the front of the back hip and your upper back open up
bad: Rushing the reach before the hips have dropped

good: Tall hips, and strike the ground right underneath you
Feel a light, springy bounce off the ball of the foot
bad: Reaching the foot out in front of your body

exercises.name: Build-Up Run
exercises.note: Run the last two as ten metres out, a turn at about three quarters speed and ten metres back.

good: Each one a little faster than the last, and the final one at about nine tenths of top speed
Feel fast but relaxed, never straining
bad: Going flat out on the first one

exercises.name: Shuttle Sprint
exercises.note: Game 1 of 4: if your turns get sloppy, a foot slips, something twinges or your sprints slow right down, stop after this game and go to the cool-down.

good: Sprint to the line, plant and turn, then drive straight back out
Feel your whole foot push into the floor on every turn
bad: Planting with a stiff leg way out in front of your body

exercises.name: Shuttle Sprint
exercises.note: Game 2 of 4: walk and breathe for ninety seconds first, and go to the cool-down instead if the last game got sloppy, twinged or slowed right down.
